---README---
# Unfinished Business

**Bring your ideas to life.**

A local browser companion built on OpenCode's open-source coding harness. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea through an approved plan, real implementation, verification, and submission drafts.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea and approve a useful product scope |
| Architect | Present one planning section, revise it, and wait for approval before continuing |
| Maker | Use OpenCode to perform approved work and show actual results |
| Witness | Review evidence and prepare honest final materials |

OpenCode provides the agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the workshop interface, stage progression, versioned approvals, decision history, and evidence views.

## Status

Prompt 2 is active. Foundation is `14fc6a6`, Workflow is `abf87f7`, and Experience is `b465fa0`. The Verification phase has entered local reconciliation: typecheck, production build, all 21 tests, and the production dependency audit pass. Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness run through OpenCode's free DeepSeek route. Maker edits only an isolated demo workspace, then the app runs `node --test` there. A live umbrella-relay attempt wrote a ledger whose Node check failed on a duplicate `snapshot` declaration; Witness recorded that failure. Sentry error, performance, replay, feedback, profiling, and metadata-only OpenCode agent tracing are verified locally. Backboard remains dependent on its API/tooling setup.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

In another terminal, `npm run build && npm start` serves the built workshop and API on `127.0.0.1`. Set `UB_PORT` if `4200` is taken. `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:4096`. The server scripts and Vite read the gitignored `.env`; use `.env.example` as the safe template. Start `opencode serve` yourself; this app does not print or store its password. Project data stays in `UB_DATA_DIR` (default `.unfinished-business/`), which is gitignored.

Environment setup, Sentry release/source-map configuration, and OpenCode password matching are documented in [docs/SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md](docs/SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md).

Render deployment and its required secrets are documented in [docs/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md). The hosted service is password protected and uses a persistent disk; it is not compatible with Render's free plan.

Run the dependency-free diagnostic from the repository:

```bash
node scripts/preflight.mjs
```

It checks the toolchain, read-only Git state, DNS, localhost socket access and Entire status. A temporary localhost listener closes immediately. OpenCode version/help use disposable temporary storage, without changing existing sessions or credentials. It performs no inference, installs, account setup, capture setup or Git writes. Exit code 1 means a blocking diagnostic failed; exit code 0 is only preflight, never a passing integration proof. See the blueprint's execution record for the tested result and resume conditions.

- [Engineering blueprint](docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — canonical implementation plan and amendments.
- [Product idea packet](docs/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved product scope and updated decisions.
- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — Prompts 0–3 and current project overrides.
- [Project Prompt 1](docs/prompts/PROMPT_1_ARCHITECT.md) — complete project-specific Architect instructions with section-by-section review.

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Steps are work/checklist units, not individual commits. Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.

The Experience gate is committed and linked to Entire checkpoint `01M6874YH3592P2RKCZ9KV0MVQ`. The active unit is Verification V1 partner access: Backboard and Sentry work waits for supported credentials/tooling or an approved focused amendment. Publication and submission belong to Prompt 3.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence.

372:         const key = callKey(input.sessionID, input.callID)
373:         // A new call under this key: some providers number calls per
374:         // conversation, so an earlier call's markers must not dedupe or
375:         // swallow this one's start and stop.
376:         announcedTasks.delete(key)
377:         stoppedBeforeStart.delete(key)
378:         stoppedOnError.delete(key)
379:         taskStartedAt.set(key, Date.now())
380:       } catch {
381:         // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
382:       }
383:     },
384:     // Subagent completion. tool.execute.after for the task tool fires once, with
385:     // the child session ID in output.metadata: at true completion for a
386:     // foreground task, immediately for a background one (metadata.background),
387:     // whose stop is held until the child goes idle. Synchronous: `opencode run`
388:     // exits on the parent's idle right after this, and an async hook would be
389:     // killed before it finished.
390:     "tool.execute.after": async (input, output) => {
391:       try {
392:         if (input.tool !== "task") return
393:         const key = callKey(input.sessionID, input.callID)
394:         const announced = takeLiveTask(key)
395:         if (stoppedOnError.delete(key) && !announced) {
396:           // Already stopped: its part ended in error first.
397:           taskStartedAt.delete(key)
398:           return
399:         }
400:         // A failed command subtask fires this hook with no output; its
401:         // announced child still ends here.
402:         const childID = output?.metadata?.sessionId ?? announced?.subagent_id
403:         if (!childID) {
404:           taskStartedAt.delete(key)
405:           return
406:         }
407:         trackChild(childID, input.sessionID)
408:         const startedAt = taskStartedAt.get(key) ?? 0
409:         taskStartedAt.delete(key)
410:         if (!announced) stoppedBeforeStart.add(key)
411:         // A child's own task call (subagent_depth > 1) is recorded on the
412:         // top-level session: the child has no Entire session of its own.
413:         const payload = announced ?? {
414:           session_id: topLevelSession(input.sessionID),
415:           tool_use_id: input.callID,
416:           subagent_id: childID,
417:           subagent_type: input.args?.subagent_type ?? "",
418:           task_description: input.args?.description ?? "",
419:           started_at: startedAt,
420:         }
421:         if (output?.metadata?.background === true) {
422:           backgroundTasks.set(childID, [...(backgroundTasks.get(childID) ?? []), payload])
423:           return
424:         }
425:         callHookSync("subagent-stop", payload)
426:       } catch {
427:         // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
428:       }
429:     },
430:     event: async ({ event }) => {
431:       try {
432:         const props = (event as any).properties
433:         const info = props?.info
434:         if (event.type.startsWith("session.") && info?.parentID && info?.id) trackChild(info.id, info.parentID)
435:         if (event.type === "message.part.updated") {
436:           announceTask(props?.part)
437:           stopFailedTask(props?.part)
438:           const part = props?.part
439:           // Only a part in a tracked session: synthetic text also carries
440:           // attachment contents, which could spell the same envelope.
441:           const sid = part?.sessionID
442:           const tracked = sid === currentSessionID || childSessions.has(sid) || [...parentOf.values()].includes(sid)
443:           if (tracked && part?.type === "text" && part.synthetic === true && typeof part.text === "string") {
444:             const result = backgroundResult.exec(part.text)
445:             if (result) drainBackgroundTasks(result[1])
446:           }
447:         }
448:         // An aborted message, reported on session.error, or on the message
449:         // itself when the run was interrupted outside the processor.
450:         if (event.type === "session.error" && props?.error?.name === "MessageAbortedError" && props?.sessionID) {
451:           backgroundSessionAborted(props.sessionID)
452:         }
453:         if (event.type === "message.updated" && info?.error?.name === "MessageAbortedError" && info?.sessionID) {
454:           backgroundSessionAborted(info.sessionID)
455:         }
456:         if (event.type === "session.status" && props?.sessionID) {
457:           if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") busySessions.add(props.sessionID)
458:           else if (busySessions.delete(props.sessionID)) {
459:             if (drainAtIdle.delete(props.sessionID)) drainBackgroundTasks(props.sessionID)
460:             else finishBackgroundTask(props.sessionID)
461:           }
462:         }
463:         const eventSessionID: string | undefined =
464:           props?.sessionID ?? info?.sessionID ?? info?.id ?? props?.part?.sessionID
465:         if (eventSessionID && childSessions.has(eventSessionID)) return
466:         switch (event.type) {
467:           case "session.created": {
468:             const session = info
469:             if (!session?.id) break
470:             // Reset per-session tracking state when switching sessions.
471:             if (resetSessionTracking(session.id)) {
472:               await callHook("session-start", {
473:                 session_id: session.id,
474:               })
475:             }
476:             break
477:           }
478: 
479:           case "message.updated": {
480:             const msg = info
481:             if (!msg) break
482: 
483:             if (msg.sessionID && resetSessionTracking(msg.sessionID)) {
484:               callHookSync("session-start", {
485:                 session_id: msg.sessionID,
486:               })
487:             }
488: 
489:             // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
490:             messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
491:             // Track model from assistant messages
492:             if (msg.role === "assistant" && msg.modelID) {
493:               currentModel = msg.modelID
494:             }
495: 
496:             // Fallback: some opencode run flows commit before any message.part.updated
497:             // event is delivered for the user's prompt. Start the turn from the
498:             // user message itself so git hooks see an ACTIVE session in time.
499:             if (msg.role === "user" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
500:               seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
501:               const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
502:               if (sessionID) {
503:                 fireTurnStart({
504:                   session_id: sessionID,
505:                   prompt: "",
506:                   model: currentModel ?? "",
507:                 })
508:               }
509:             }
510:             break
511:           }
512: 
513:           case "message.part.updated": {
514:             const part = props?.part
515:             if (!part?.messageID) break
516: 
517:             // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
518:             const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
519:             if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
520:               seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
521:               const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
522:               if (sessionID) {
523:                 // A synthetic part is OpenCode writing, not the user: a
524:                 // background task's result arrives this way. The parent does
525:                 // take a turn on it, so the turn still starts, with no prompt.
526:                 fireTurnStart({
527:                   session_id: sessionID,
528:                   prompt: part.synthetic === true ? "" : (part.text ?? ""),
529:                   model: currentModel ?? "",
530:                 })
531:               }
532:             }
533: 
534:             break
535:           }
536: 
537:           case "session.status": {
538:             // session.status fires in both TUI and non-interactive (run) mode.
539:             // session.idle is deprecated and not reliably emitted in run mode.
540:             if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
541:             const sessionID = props?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
542:             if (!sessionID) break
543:             // Use sync variant: `opencode run` exits on the same idle event,
544:             // so an async hook would be killed before completing.
545:             callHookSync("turn-end", {
546:               session_id: sessionID,
547:               model: currentModel ?? "",
548:             })
549:             break
550:           }
551: 
552:           case "session.compacted": {
553:             const sessionID = props?.sessionID
554:             if (!sessionID) break
555:             await callHook("compaction", {
556:               session_id: sessionID,
557:             })
558:             break
559:           }
560: 
561:           case "session.deleted": {
562:             const session = info
563:             if (!session?.id) break
564:             seenUserMessages.clear()
565:             messageStore.clear()
566:             currentSessionID = null
567:             pendingInjection = null
568:             // childSessions/announcedTasks are NOT cleared here: a child's own
569:             // deletion never reaches this case (the guard above returns first),
570:             // so this only ever fires for an unrelated top-level session, and
571:             // clearing here would drop a live child back to top-level mid-task.
572:             // Use sync variant: session-end may fire during shutdown.
573:             callHookSync("session-end", {
574:               session_id: session.id,
575:             })
576:             break
577:           }
578: 
579:           case "server.instance.disposed": {
580:             // Fires when OpenCode shuts down (TUI close or `opencode run` exit).
581:             // session.deleted only fires on explicit user deletion, not on quit,
582:             // so this is the only reliable way to end sessions on exit.
583:             if (!currentSessionID) break
584:             const sessionID = currentSessionID
585:             seenUserMessages.clear()
586:             messageStore.clear()
587:             currentSessionID = null
588:             pendingInjection = null
589:             childSessions.clear()
590:             rootOf.clear()
591:             parentOf.clear()
592:             announcedTasks.clear()
593:             taskStartedAt.clear()
594:             liveTasks.clear()
595:             partCallID.clear()
596:             stoppedBeforeStart.clear()
597:             stoppedOnError.clear()
598:             // A background child still running here is ended by the Go side's
599:             // SessionEnd sweep, which completes every live task record.
600:             backgroundTasks.clear()
601:             busySessions.clear()
602:             drainAtIdle.clear()
603:             // Use sync variant: this is the last event before process exit.
604:             callHookSync("session-end", {
605:               session_id: sessionID,
606:             })
607:             break
608:           }
609:         }
610:       } catch {
611:         // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
612:       }
613:     },
614:   }
615: }

617: // OpenCode 2 plugin.
618: //
619: // OpenCode 2 runs plugins inside a background service shared by every
620: // repository, so this differs from the OpenCode 1 plugin in three ways:
621: //   - Hooks (prompt, context, tool) are per location, but the event stream
622: //     is process-wide and execution events carry no location. Only sessions
623: //     this instance saw in its own prompt hook are acted on; nothing falls
624: //     back to a "current" session.
625: //   - Nothing blocks: a synchronous spawn would stall every session in the
626: //     service. Hooks that must finish first (session-start, turn-start,
627: //     subagent start/stop) are awaited asynchronous spawns with a timeout.
628: //   - `opencode run --standalone` kills plugin cleanup about 3s after the
629: //     turn ends, so turn-end, session-end and held subagent stops run detached
630: //     and outlive it, each after the session's earlier detached hooks.
631: // A turn is one execution: a prompt sent while one runs joins it, so turn-start
632: // fires only when the session has no active turn (later prompts are read from
633: // the transcript). OpenCode 1 also calls setup, with a reduced context; the
634: // guard below leaves it to EntirePlugin.
635: 
636: // Awaited hooks give up after this long rather than hang the shared service.
637: const v2HookTimeoutMs = 60_000
638: // Cleanup waits this long for the final turn-end and session-end, inside the
639: // ~3s `opencode run --standalone` allows it, so a run's session-end lands
640: // before the next run's turn-start. Hooks still running then finish detached.
641: const v2CleanupWaitMs = 2_500
642: // A detached hook waits at most this many 0.1s polls for the hooks before it.
643: const v2DetachedWaitPolls = 1_200
644: 
645: // The shared service may have been started from a shell with a repository
646: // selected through the environment; hooks for this location must resolve
647: // their own repository from their working directory.
648: const v2RepoSelectorEnv = ["GIT_DIR", "GIT_COMMON_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_INDEX_FILE"]
649: 
650: async function entireSetup(ctx: any) {
651:   if (!(ctx?.session?.hook && ctx?.tool?.hook && ctx?.event?.subscribe && ctx?.location?.directory)) return
652:   const directory: string = ctx.location.directory
653:   const hookEnv: Record<string, string | undefined> = { ...process.env }
654:   for (const key of v2RepoSelectorEnv) delete hookEnv[key]
655: 
656:   // Top-level sessions seen in this instance's prompt hook.
657:   const sessions = new Set<string>()
658:   // Sessions session-start has been sent for.
659:   const startedSessions = new Set<string>()
660:   // Top-level sessions with a turn started and not yet ended.
661:   const activeTurns = new Set<string>()
662:   // Session -> model ID of its latest LLM call (from the context hook).
663:   const models = new Map<string, string>()
664:   // Session -> one-time context injection from turn-start, applied on the
665:   // session's next LLM call.
666:   const pendingInjection = new Map<string, string>()
667:   // Session -> its detached hooks still running (turn-end, session-end,
668:   // compaction, held subagent stops). Each new detached hook waits for these
669:   // by PID (it may outlive this process) and the next turn-start awaits them,
670:   // so a session's hooks land in the order OpenCode 1 sends them.
671:   const inflight = new Map<string, Set<{ done: Promise<void>; pid?: number }>>()
672:   // Session -> held subagent stops released but still waiting for their
673:   // call's subagent-start, before they become detached hooks. Counted from
674:   // the moment they are released, so neither session-end nor the next
675:   // turn-start can overtake them.
676:   const pendingStops = new Map<string, Set<Promise<void>>>()
677:   // Child (subagent) sessions: child -> top-level session, child -> launcher.
678:   const rootOf = new Map<string, string>()
679:   const parentOf = new Map<string, string>()
680:   // Per subagent call, keyed by callKey(calling session, callID). A callID is
681:   // unique only within its session.
682:   const taskCalls = new Map<string, { startedAt: number; input: any }>()
683:   // Call key -> its subagent-start, which every stop of the call awaits; it
684:   // also marks the call announced, so a late progress update cannot announce
685:   // it again. Cleared when a new call reuses the key.
686:   const taskStarts = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
687:   // Announced calls not yet stopped: call key -> subagent-stop payload.
688:   const liveTasks = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>()
689:   // Calls stopped before their running progress was seen; a late progress
690:   // update must not announce a call that already stopped.
691:   const stoppedBeforeStart = new Set<string>()
692:   // Background children: child -> held calls, oldest first. Each of the
693:   // child's executions ends the oldest held call (a resumed call that joins a
694:   // running child queues behind it as its own execution).
695:   const backgroundTasks = new Map<string, { key: string; payload: Record<string, unknown> }[]>()
696:   // Children with an execution running; children whose held calls all end
697:   // when that execution ends (their launcher was interrupted); and children
698:   // whose execution ended with no call held yet (a launch result that arrives
699:   // late), so the call that arrives next ends at once.
700:   const busySessions = new Set<string>()
701:   const drainAtEnd = new Set<string>()
702:   const endedUnheld = new Set<string>()
703:   // Top-level session -> its pending event handling (see enqueueEvent).
704:   const eventQueues = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
705: 
706:   function callKey(sessionID: string, callID: string): string {
707:     return sessionID + "\0" + callID
708:   }
709: 
710:   // within resolves when p settles or after ms, whichever is first. The timer
711:   // also keeps the process alive while waiting on an unref'd detached hook.
712:   function within(p: Promise<unknown>, ms: number): Promise<void> {
713:     return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
714:       const timer = setTimeout(resolve, ms)
715:       p.finally(() => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve() })
716:     })
717:   }
718: 
719:   function isChild(sessionID: string): boolean {
720:     return rootOf.has(sessionID)
721:   }
722: 
723:   function tracked(sessionID: string | undefined): sessionID is string {
724:     return !!sessionID && (sessions.has(sessionID) || isChild(sessionID))
725:   }
726: 
727:   function topLevelSession(sessionID: string): string {
728:     return rootOf.get(sessionID) ?? sessionID
729:   }
730: 
731:   function trackChild(childID: string, parentID: string) {
732:     if (!rootOf.has(childID)) rootOf.set(childID, rootOf.get(parentID) ?? parentID)
733:     if (!parentOf.has(childID)) parentOf.set(childID, parentID)
734:   }
735: 
736:   // runHook pipes the payload to a hook and resolves with its stdout. Errors
737:   // and timeouts resolve with "" — plugin failures must not break OpenCode.
738:   function runHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<string> {
739:     return new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
740:       try {
741:         const [cmd, ...args] = hookCmd(hookName)
742:         const proc = spawn(cmd, args, { cwd: directory, env: hookEnv, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "ignore"] })
743:         let out = ""
744:         const timer = setTimeout(() => {
745:           try { proc.kill() } catch {}
746:           resolve(out)
747:         }, v2HookTimeoutMs)
748:         proc.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8")
749:         proc.stdout?.on("data", (chunk: string) => { out += chunk })
750:         proc.on("error", () => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(out) })
751:         proc.on("close", () => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(out) })
752:         proc.stdin?.on("error", () => {})
753:         proc.stdin?.end(JSON.stringify(payload) + "\n")
754:       } catch {
755:         resolve("")
756:       }
757:     })
758:   }
759: 
760:   // runDetached starts a session's hook in its own process group so it
761:   // survives OpenCode exiting, after the session's detached hooks still
762:   // running (it polls their PIDs, bounded). done settles if this process
763:   // lives to see the hook finish.
764:   function runDetached(sessionID: string, hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
765:     const running = inflight.get(sessionID) ?? new Set()
766:     inflight.set(sessionID, running)
767:     const pids = [...running].map((h) => h.pid).filter((pid): pid is number => typeof pid === "number")
768:     const entry: { done: Promise<void>; pid?: number } = { done: Promise.resolve() }
769:     entry.done = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
770:       try {
771:         let [cmd, ...args] = hookCmd(hookName)
772:         if (pids.length > 0) {
773:           const wait = `for p in ${pids.join(" ")}; do i=0; while kill -0 $p 2>/dev/null && [ $i -lt ${v2DetachedWaitPolls} ]; do sleep 0.1; i=$((i+1)); done; done`
774:           args = ["-c", `${wait}; ${args[1]}`]
775:         }
776:         const proc = spawn(cmd, args, { cwd: directory, env: hookEnv, stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"], detached: true })
777:         entry.pid = proc.pid
778:         proc.on("error", () => resolve())
779:         proc.on("close", () => resolve())
780:         proc.stdin?.on("error", () => {})
781:         proc.stdin?.end(JSON.stringify(payload) + "\n")
782:         proc.unref()
783:       } catch {
784:         resolve()
785:       }
786:     }).then(() => { running.delete(entry) })
787:     running.add(entry)
788:     return entry.done
789:   }
790: 
791:   // settled resolves once the session's detached hooks, including held
792:   // stops not yet started, have finished.
793:   function settled(sessionID: string): Promise<void> {
794:     const waits = [...(pendingStops.get(sessionID) ?? [])]
795:     for (const h of inflight.get(sessionID) ?? []) waits.push(h.done)
796:     if (waits.length === 0) return Promise.resolve()
797:     return within(Promise.all(waits), v2HookTimeoutMs)
798:   }
799: 
800:   // classify records whether a session is top-level or a child, asking
801:   // OpenCode for its parent the first time. A child's prompt reaches the hook
802:   // before any event names its parent, so events cannot answer this in time.
803:   async function classify(sessionID: string): Promise<"top" | "child" | "unknown"> {
804:     if (sessions.has(sessionID)) return "top"
805:     if (isChild(sessionID)) return "child"
806:     try {
807:       const session: any = await ctx.session.get({ sessionID })
808:       if (session?.parentID) {
809:         trackChild(sessionID, session.parentID)
810:         return "child"
811:       }
812:       if (!session) return "unknown"
813:     } catch {
814:       return "unknown"
815:     }
816:     sessions.add(sessionID)
817:     return "top"
818:   }
819: 
820:   async function startTurn(sessionID: string, prompt: string) {
821:     activeTurns.add(sessionID)
822:     await settled(sessionID)
823:     if (!startedSessions.has(sessionID)) {
824:       startedSessions.add(sessionID)
825:       await runHook("session-start", { session_id: sessionID })
826:     }
827:     const out = await runHook("turn-start", { session_id: sessionID, prompt, model: models.get(sessionID) ?? "" })
828:     const injected = parseInjectedContext(out)
829:     if (injected) pendingInjection.set(sessionID, injected)
830:   }
831: 
832:   function endTurn(sessionID: string) {
833:     if (!activeTurns.delete(sessionID)) return
834:     runDetached(sessionID, "turn-end", { session_id: sessionID, model: models.get(sessionID) ?? "" })
835:   }
836: 
837:   function taskPayload(sessionID: string, callID: string, childID: string, call?: { startedAt: number; input: any }, input?: any) {
838:     const args = call?.input ?? input ?? {}
839:     return {
840:       session_id: topLevelSession(sessionID),
841:       tool_use_id: callID,
842:       subagent_id: childID,
843:       subagent_type: args.agent ?? args.subagent_type ?? "",
844:       task_description: args.description ?? "",
845:       started_at: call?.startedAt ?? 0,
846:     }
847:   }
848: 
849:   // announceTask sends subagent-start once per call and records it, so every
850:   // stop path can wait for it.
851:   function announceTask(key: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
852:     const existing = taskStarts.get(key)
853:     if (existing) return existing
854:     const started = runHook("subagent-start", payload).then(() => {})
855:     taskStarts.set(key, started)
856:     return started
857:   }
858: 
859:   // A held stop runs detached (the child can end as OpenCode exits), after
860:   // its call's start and the session's earlier detached hooks.
861:   function stopHeldTask(held: { key: string; payload: Record<string, unknown> }) {
862:     const sessionID = held.payload.session_id as string
863:     const pending = pendingStops.get(sessionID) ?? new Set()
864:     pendingStops.set(sessionID, pending)
865:     const stop: Promise<void> = (async () => {
866:       const started = taskStarts.get(held.key)
867:       if (started) await within(started, v2HookTimeoutMs)
868:       // Registered as a detached hook before leaving pendingStops, so there is
869:       // no moment where neither set holds it.
870:       const done = runDetached(sessionID, "subagent-stop", held.payload)
871:       pending.delete(stop)
872:       await done
873:     })()
874:     pending.add(stop)
875:   }
876: 
877:   function finishBackgroundTask(childID: string) {
878:     const held = backgroundTasks.get(childID)
879:     const next = held?.shift()
880:     if (!next) {
881:       endedUnheld.add(childID)
882:       return
883:     }
884:     if (held!.length === 0) backgroundTasks.delete(childID)
885:     stopHeldTask(next)
886:   }
887: 
888:   function drainBackgroundTasks(childID: string) {
889:     const held = backgroundTasks.get(childID)
890:     if (!held) {
891:       endedUnheld.add(childID)
892:       return
893:     }
894:     backgroundTasks.delete(childID)
895:     for (const next of held) stopHeldTask(next)
896:   }
897: 
898:   // An interrupted session ends the held calls of the children it launched:
899:   // at once for an idle child, when its execution ends for a busy one.
900:   function launcherInterrupted(sessionID: string) {
901:     for (const [childID, parentID] of parentOf) {
902:       if (parentID !== sessionID || !backgroundTasks.has(childID)) continue
903:       if (busySessions.has(childID)) drainAtEnd.add(childID)
904:       else drainBackgroundTasks(childID)
905:     }
906:   }
907: 
908:   // endSession ends the session after its held stops have become detached
909:   // hooks, so session-end waits for them by PID. Calls still held for its
910:   // children end with it (a child whose end arrived before it was tracked

# Entire CLI [Entire](https://entire.com) is a Git forge built for agent–human collaboration. This CLI is how you and your agents use Entire from the terminal — anything you do on entire.com, you can do here: - **Distributed Git hosting** — host repositories on Entire's Git-compatible server, or mirror your GitHub ones, and replicate them in regions around the world for data residency and the scale of agent traffic. → [Repositories & Git Hosting](#repositories--git-hosting) - **Trails** — instead of reviewing a diff, get a heads-up display for every change, with customizable evals that agents score on every push. → [Trails](#trails) - **Continuous memory** — capture every agent session as a checkpoint linked to your commits; [entire-brain](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview) combines them with [entire-graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview)'s code map into project memory. → [Agent Sessions](#agent-sessions) Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, Factory AI Droid, Pi, and [more](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview), and extends through [plugins](#plugins). Pushes through a GitHub mirror still trigger your GitHub Actions, and Trails can also show CI results from Buildkite and Depot. Open source under the MIT license. Docs: **[docs.entire.com](https://docs.entire.com)**. ## Contents - [Install](#install) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Repositories & Git Hosting](#repositories--git-hosting) - [Trails](#trails) - [Agent Sessions](#agent-sessions) - [Search, Activity & the API](#search-activity--the-api) - [Plugins](#plugins) - [Security & Privacy](#security--privacy) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Documentation](#documentation) ## Install ```bash brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire # macOS and Linux curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash # macOS and Linux, without Homebrew irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell 5.1+ ``` For the nightly channel (prerelease builds with the latest changes): ```bash brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly iex "& {$(irm https://entire.com/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly" ``` Requires Git on macOS, Linux, or Windows. Scoop, `go install`, and installing during a GitHub outage are covered in [Installation](https://docs.entire.com/installation). ## Quick Start **1. Capture agent sessions** — works in any Git repository, no account needed: ```bash cd your-project entire enable # pick your agents; installs their hooks and Entire's git hooks entire status # current sessions and where checkpoints are uploaded ``` **2. Put a repository on Entire** — sign in, then mirror a GitHub repository into one or more clusters, or create an Entire-native one. Mirroring needs the [Entire GitHub App](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/github-app-access) installed for that repository. ```bash entire login entire repo mirror add # wizard: pick repos and clusters entire repo clone /gh// --nearest entire project create # wizard: owner, name, region entire repo create --project entire repo clone /et// ``` Then `cd` into the clone and run `entire enable` there to capture sessions in it. **3. Open a Trail** — in a repository on Entire, on the branch you're working on: ```bash git switch -c add-rate-limiting entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting" entire trail show ``` ## Repositories & Git Hosting Entire hosts Git repositories on clusters in several regions, so agents can clone, fetch, and push against a copy near where they run. - **Region** — where an organization's or project's data stays: a jurisdiction such as `us` or `eu`, set with `--region` when you create it. - **Cluster** — an Entire Git host, such as `aws-eu-central-1.entire.io`. `entire cluster list` shows them; a repository can have copies on several. - **Project** — holds Entire-native repositories and belongs to an organization or a personal account. Repository and project commands take its plain name (`--project acme`); Trail commands take `et/`, and treat a GitHub owner as the project for its mirrors (`gh/`). - **Mirror** — a copy of a repository on one cluster. GitHub repositories are mirrored from their GitHub upstream, and native repositories can be mirrored to more clusters. `entire repo mirror` manages both. Repository references name their forge: `/et//` for an Entire-native repository, `/gh//` for a GitHub mirror, or a full `entire:///…` clone URL. ```bash entire repo create web --project acme # Entire-native, private by default entire repo mirror add /gh/acme/web --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io entire repo clone /gh/acme/web --nearest # time each cluster and use the fastest entire repo remote add entire # add Entire to an existing checkout, beside origin ``` A GitHub mirror keeps GitHub as the source of truth: clones and fetches come from Entire, and pushes are forwarded to GitHub, where your GitHub permissions, branch protection, and required checks still apply. Clones use `entire://` URLs through the `git-remote-entire` helper that ships with the packaged installs; after that, it is plain Git. See [Repositories](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/overview) and [Mirrors in the CLI](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors-in-cli) for regions, mirroring, unmirrored branches, moving a mirror off GitHub, branch protection, and access. ## Trails A **Trail** follows a change from intent to merge. Instead of reviewing a diff, you get a heads-up display for it — the Trail's page on entire.com, or `entire trail show` and `entire trail watch` here — with findings from evals that agents score on every push. Each Trail has a number in its project, such as `#42`. ```bash entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting" --type feature # publishes the current branch entire trail list --project et/acme --status open entire trail show # the Trail for the current branch entire trail watch # stream reviews, findings, and runner events live entire trail finding # findings dashboard for this branch entire trail finding apply # apply a finding's suggested fix entire trail finding resolve -m "fixed in abc123" entire trail comment add -m "Should this cover the admin API too?" entire trail approve entire trail merge # merge this branch's change into its base entire trail resume 42 # continue Trail #42: restore its branch's sessions in your agent ``` Trail commands use the current repository's project (`gh/` or `et/`); pass `--project` or `--repo` to work on another one without a checkout. `entire trail list` always takes `--project`. Other subcommands are `checkout`, `link`, `unlink`, `update`, and `approvals`. **Project agents** are those evals: review agents such as risk, confidence, drift, security, and review, configured per project in Entire, which score each push to a Trail and raise its findings. `entire project agent` lists them and adds Entire's presets to your repository with `add`. Preset agents run on free credit; a custom agent runs once the project's billing is set up. ## Agent Sessions `entire enable` connects your agents and installs Entire's git hooks, keeping any hooks you already have. Use your agent and commit as usual: each commit that includes agent work gets a **checkpoint** — the prompts, transcript, and files touched — linked to the commit by an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Entire never adds commits to your branch; by default, checkpoints are stored as their own Git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/…`) and pushed alongside your code. ```bash entire checkpoint list # checkpoints on this branch entire checkpoint explain # the prompt, transcript, and files behind a checkpoint entire session resume # restore a branch's sessions and continue in your agent entire agent add # add an agent later; entire configure for other settings entire disable # turn capture off (--uninstall removes Entire from the repo) ``` See [Sessions](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/overview) and [Checkpoint Storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage) for how capture works and migrating from legacy branch storage, [Settings](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/settings-layers) and [Git Hooks](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/git-hooks) for configuration, and [Checkpoint Destination](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-destination) for choosing the remote or a [separate checkpoint repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/store-checkpoints-in-another-repo). Checkpoints are also the raw material for continuous memory: [entire-brain](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview), installed separately, combines them with [entire-graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview)'s code map into project memory your agents can query. From the CLI, `entire search` and `entire checkpoint explain` are the way in. ## Search, Activity & the API - **Search** — `entire search` runs hybrid (semantic + keyword) search over checkpoints, commits, and sessions, scoped to the current repo or `--all-repos`. `--json --compact` returns a trimmed shape suited to agents, and `entire checkpoint explain ` fetches the full detail of a hit. - **Activity and dispatches** — `entire activity` shows your activity overview, repository breakdown, and recent sessions from entire.com. `entire dispatch` writes a summary of recent agent work; `--local` generates it with your locally installed agent CLI instead of the Entire server. - **Raw API access** — `entire api ` makes an authenticated request to an Entire API and prints the JSON response, like `gh api`. It attaches your token and picks the host: `--to core` (the default) reaches the control plane (orgs, projects, repos, mirrors, clusters), `--to cell` reaches your home data cell (activity, repo aggregates), and `--jurisdiction ` reaches another jurisdiction's cell. `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{repo_id}` in the path are filled from the current repository's `origin`; `{repo_id}` needs a GitHub repository with an active Entire mirror. These endpoints are internal and can change without notice; where a purpose-built command exists, prefer it. ```bash entire api /api/v1/clusters entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}" entire api /api/v1/me ``` ## Plugins Any executable named `entire-` on `$PATH` runs as `entire `. Install plugins from the [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) or any Git host: ```bash entire plugin search entire plugin install entire plugin list ``` Installs from a Git host are verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. See [`entire plugin`](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/plugin). ## Security & Privacy **Session transcripts are pushed to your Git remote** — as checkpoint refs, not commits on your branch. If that repository is public, anyone can read them. Entire redacts detected secrets before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best effort; `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` shows what your next push will upload, and `entire checkpoint explain ` shows a checkpoint's contents. To keep transcripts out of a public repository, upload them to a separate private repository (`entire configure --local --checkpoint-remote github:/`) or stop uploading them (`entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions`). `entire enable` names the checkpoint destination every time it runs. See [Security](https://docs.entire.com/security) for redaction, scanners, deleting checkpoints, and cleaning up data from older versions. ## Troubleshooting | Issue | Solution | | --- | --- | | "Not a git repository" | Navigate to a Git repository first | | "Entire is disabled" | Run `entire enable` | | Agent hooks outdated after a CLI upgrade | Run `entire agent add `; add `--force` if that does not fix them | | A session stuck ACTIVE, or leftover session state | Run `entire doctor`, then `entire clean --force` if it persists | | Anything else | Run `entire doctor`; `entire doctor bundle` produces a redacted diagnostic bundle for a bug report | Set `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` for debug logs, and `ACCESSIBLE=1` for screen-reader-friendly prompts. Headless servers and CI: see [`entire login`](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/login). ## Documentation - **[docs.entire.com](https://docs.entire.com)** — guides for Entire and the CLI, including [how the CLI and entire.com fit together](https://docs.entire.com/platforms/cli-and-entire-com) - `entire help`, `entire --help`, and the [CLI reference](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference); `entire agent-help` is the version written for coding agents - **Issues:** https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues · **Contributing:** [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## License MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# OpenCode

> Capture OpenCode transcripts, file changes, tool calls, and token usage with Entire

The OpenCode integration uses a project-level TypeScript plugin.

Follow [Set Up an Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/setup.md) for shared installation, verification, and troubleshooting steps.

## Add OpenCode

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add opencode
opencode
```

Entire writes `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. The plugin captures session and turn events, then uses `opencode export` to materialize the full conversation, file changes, tool calls, and token usage.

OpenCode supports commits before a turn ends. Entire refreshes the exported transcript so a checkpoint created mid-turn includes the agent activity available at that point.

## Limitations

OpenCode does not expose subagent lifecycle events. Entire captures the main session. `entire import` cannot import existing OpenCode sessions.

## Resume

`entire session resume BRANCH` restores the recorded session data when needed and prints:

```bash theme={null}
opencode -s SESSION_ID
```

See the [`session resume` command reference](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/session#session-resume) for flags and additional behavior.

=== attach help ===
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away (under the manual
    checkpoint push policy it waits for 'entire checkpoint push'). The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

# Plugins

Write your own plugins to extend OpenCode.

Plugins allow you to extend OpenCode by hooking into various events and customizing behavior. You can create plugins to add new features, integrate with external services, or modify OpenCode’s default behavior.

For examples, check out the [plugins](/docs/ecosystem#plugins) created by the community.

---

## [Use a plugin](#use-a-plugin)

There are two ways to load plugins.

---

### [From local files](#from-local-files)

Place JavaScript or TypeScript files in the plugin directory.

- `.opencode/plugins/` \- Project-level plugins

- `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` \- Global plugins

Files in these directories are automatically loaded at startup.

---

### [From npm](#from-npm)

Specify npm packages in your config file.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "plugin": ["opencode-helicone-session", "opencode-wakatime", "@my-org/custom-plugin"]}
```

Both regular and scoped npm packages are supported.

Browse available plugins in the [ecosystem](/docs/ecosystem#plugins).

---

### [How plugins are installed](#how-plugins-are-installed)

**npm plugins** are installed automatically using Bun at startup. Packages and their dependencies are cached in `~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/`.

**Local plugins** are loaded directly from the plugin directory. To use external packages, you must create a `package.json` within your config directory (see [Dependencies](#dependencies)), or publish the plugin to npm and [add it to your config](/docs/config#plugins).

---

### [Load order](#load-order)

Plugins are loaded from all sources and all hooks run in sequence. The load order is:

1. Global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`)

2. Project config (`opencode.json`)

3. Global plugin directory (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/`)

4. Project plugin directory (`.opencode/plugins/`)

Duplicate npm packages with the same name and version are loaded once. However, a local plugin and an npm plugin with similar names are both loaded separately.

---

## [Create a plugin](#create-a-plugin)

A plugin is a **JavaScript/TypeScript module** that exports one or more plugin functions. Each function receives a context object and returns a hooks object.

---

### [Dependencies](#dependencies)

Local plugins and custom tools can use external npm packages. Add a `package.json` to your config directory with the dependencies you need.

.opencode/package.json

```
{  "dependencies": {    "shescape": "^2.1.0"  }}
```

OpenCode runs `bun install` at startup to install these. Your plugins and tools can then import them.

.opencode/plugins/my-plugin.ts

```
import { escape } from "shescape"
export const MyPlugin = async (ctx) => {  return {    "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {      if (input.tool === "bash") {        output.args.command = escape(output.args.command)      }    },  }}
```

---

### [Basic structure](#basic-structure)

.opencode/plugins/example.js

```
export const MyPlugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {  console.log("Plugin initialized!")
  return {    // Hook implementations go here  }}
```

The plugin function receives:

- `project`: The current project information.

- `directory`: The current working directory.

- `worktree`: The git worktree path.

- `client`: An opencode SDK client for interacting with the AI.

- `$`: Bun’s [shell API](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/shell) for executing commands.

---

### [TypeScript support](#typescript-support)

For TypeScript plugins, you can import types from the plugin package:

my-plugin.ts

```
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
export const MyPlugin: Plugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {  return {    // Type-safe hook implementations  }}
```

---

### [Events](#events)

Plugins can subscribe to events as seen below in the Examples section. Here is a list of the different events available.

#### [Command Events](#command-events)

- `command.executed`

#### [File Events](#file-events)

- `file.edited`

- `file.watcher.updated`

#### [Installation Events](#installation-events)

- `installation.updated`

#### [LSP Events](#lsp-events)

- `lsp.client.diagnostics`

- `lsp.updated`

#### [Message Events](#message-events)

- `message.part.removed`

- `message.part.updated`

- `message.removed`

- `message.updated`

#### [Permission Events](#permission-events)

- `permission.asked`

- `permission.replied`

#### [Server Events](#server-events)

- `server.connected`

#### [Session Events](#session-events)

- `session.created`

- `session.compacted`

- `session.deleted`

- `session.diff`

- `session.error`

- `session.idle`

- `session.status`

- `session.updated`

#### [Todo Events](#todo-events)

- `todo.updated`

#### [Shell Events](#shell-events)

- `shell.env`

#### [Tool Events](#tool-events)

- `tool.execute.after`

- `tool.execute.before`

#### [TUI Events](#tui-events)

- `tui.prompt.append`

- `tui.command.execute`

- `tui.toast.show`

---

## [Examples](#examples)

Here are some examples of plugins you can use to extend opencode.

---

### [Send notifications](#send-notifications)

Send notifications when certain events occur:

.opencode/plugins/notification.js

~~~
export const NotificationPlugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {  return {    event: async ({ event }) => {      // Send notification on session completion      if (event.type === "session.idle") {        await $`osascript -e 'display notification "Session completed!" with title "opencode"'`      }    },  }}
~~~

We are using `osascript` to run AppleScript on macOS. Here we are using it to send notifications.

If you’re using the OpenCode desktop app, it can send system notifications automatically when a response is ready or when a session errors.

---

### [.env protection](#env-protection)

Prevent opencode from reading `.env` files:

.opencode/plugins/env-protection.js

```
export const EnvProtection = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {  return {    "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {      if (input.tool === "read" && output.args.filePath.includes(".env")) {        throw new Error("Do not read .env files")      }    },  }}
```

---

### [Inject environment variables](#inject-environment-variables)

Inject environment variables into all shell execution (AI tools and user terminals):

.opencode/plugins/inject-env.js

```
export const InjectEnvPlugin = async () => {  return {    "shell.env": async (input, output) => {      output.env.MY_API_KEY = "REDACTED"      output.env.PROJECT_ROOT = input.cwd    },  }}
```

---

### [Custom tools](#custom-tools)

Plugins can also add custom tools to opencode:

.opencode/plugins/custom-tools.ts

~~~
import { type Plugin, tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
export const CustomToolsPlugin: Plugin = async (ctx) => {  return {    tool: {      mytool: tool({        description: "This is a custom tool",        args: {          foo: tool.schema.string(),        },        async execute(args, context) {          const { directory, worktree } = context          return `Hello ${args.foo} from ${directory} (worktree: ${worktree})`        },      }),    },  }}
~~~

The `tool` helper creates a custom tool that opencode can call. It takes a Zod schema function and returns a tool definition with:

- `description`: What the tool does

- `args`: Zod schema for the tool’s arguments

- `execute`: Function that runs when the tool is called

Your custom tools will be available to opencode alongside built-in tools.

If a plugin tool uses the same name as a built-in tool, the plugin tool takes precedence.

---

### [Logging](#logging)

Use `client.app.log()` instead of `console.log` for structured logging:

.opencode/plugins/my-plugin.ts

```
export const MyPlugin = async ({ client }) => {  await client.app.log({    body: {      service: "my-plugin",      level: "info",      message: "Plugin initialized",      extra: { foo: "bar" },    },  })}
```

Levels: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. See [SDK documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk) for details.

---

### [Compaction hooks](#compaction-hooks)

Customize the context included when a session is compacted:

.opencode/plugins/compaction.ts

~~~
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
export const CompactionPlugin: Plugin = async (ctx) => {  return {    "experimental.session.compacting": async (input, output) => {      // Inject additional context into the compaction prompt      output.context.push(`## Custom Context
Include any state that should persist across compaction:- Current task status- Important decisions made- Files being actively worked on`)    },  }}
~~~

The `experimental.session.compacting` hook fires before the LLM generates a continuation summary. Use it to inject domain-specific context that the default compaction prompt would miss.

You can also replace the compaction prompt entirely by setting `output.prompt`:

.opencode/plugins/custom-compaction.ts

~~~
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
export const CustomCompactionPlugin: Plugin = async (ctx) => {  return {    "experimental.session.compacting": async (input, output) => {      // Replace the entire compaction prompt      output.prompt = `You are generating a continuation prompt for a multi-agent swarm session.
Summarize:1. The current task and its status2. Which files are being modified and by whom3. Any blockers or dependencies between agents4. The next steps to complete the work
Format as a structured prompt that a new agent can use to resume work.`    },  }}
~~~

When `output.prompt` is set, it completely replaces the default compaction prompt. The `output.context` array is ignored in this case.

# Plugins

Add published packages, versioned packages, scoped packages, or local plugin directories to `opencode.json(c)`.

## Configure

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    "opencode-acme-plugin",
    "opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0",
    "@acme/opencode-plugin",
    "./plugins/local",
    "../shared/plugin",
    "/absolute/path/plugin",
    "file:///home/me/plugins/local",
    {
      "package": "@acme/opencode-plugin",
      "options": {
        "agent": "reviewer",
        "strict": true,
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

Relative paths resolve from the config file containing the entry.

Configured local paths must be directories. A path to a single file is skipped. See [Load](/build/plugins#load) for
how OpenCode finds each part in a directory.

Plugin arrays from applicable config files are applied from lowest to highest precedence instead of replacing one
another.

```text
~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc
./opencode.jsonc
./.opencode/opencode.jsonc
```

## Discover

OpenCode also loads direct `.ts` and `.js` files and immediate plugin package directories from every discovered
`.opencode/plugins/` directory.

```text
.opencode/
└── plugins/
    ├── concise.ts
    ├── reviewer.js
    └── acme-package/
```

Global plugins use the same discovery layout under the OpenCode config directory.

```text
~/.config/opencode/plugins/
```

A `plugins/` directory beside a project-root `opencode.json(c)` is not discovered automatically; configure its plugin
directories explicitly or move it under `.opencode/`.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["./plugins/local"]
}
```

## Control

Plugin entries are processed in order. Prefix an ID or wildcard with `-` to disable it, use `*` for every plugin, and
use `.*` to match an ID prefix. A later ID re-enables a plugin.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["*", "-opencode.provider.*", "opencode.provider.openai", "-acme.reviewer"]
}
```

Two built-in plugins ignore removals so that a repository cannot switch off
[policy](/policies) enforcement: `opencode.config.policy` and
`opencode.provider.opencode`, the Console connection that delivers organization
policy.

## Manage

Install, list, check, update, or remove global package plugins with the CLI.

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0
opencode plugin list
opencode plugin list --builtin
opencode plugin check
opencode plugin update
opencode plugin update opencode-acme-plugin
opencode plugin remove opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0
```

`plugin check` checks server, GUI-only, and TUI-only package plugins for updates. `plugin update` updates every outdated package;
pass a configured package target to check or update only that package. Local plugins and exact package revisions are
skipped.

Package installation accepts npm names with versions, tags, or ranges, plus npm-compatible Git package specifications.
Git repositories can use hosted shortcuts, HTTPS, or SSH, including private repositories available through your existing
Git credentials.

```sh
opencode plugin add @acme/opencode-plugin@latest
opencode plugin add github:acme/opencode-plugin
opencode plugin add git+ssh://git@github.com/acme/opencode-plugin.git#main
opencode plugin add 'github:acme/plugins#main::path:packages/opencode-plugin'
```

Branches, tags, complete commit hashes, and npm's `::path:` repository-subdirectory selectors are supported. Configure
local paths directly; tarball and npm alias targets are not accepted by `plugin add`.

## Reload

Changes under watched config directories reload automatically. Server startup loads cached package plugins immediately,
installs missing packages in the background, and checks unpinned npm and Git plugins for updates without changing the
installed package. Exact npm versions and full Git commit hashes stay pinned. Changes to unwatched local dependencies
may still require restarting OpenCode.

```sh
touch .opencode/plugins/concise/index.ts
opencode service restart
```

## Desktop

A plugin that exports `./gui-experimental` also adds panels, commands, or settings to OpenCode Desktop. The app loads
plugins from the server it runs, so configure the plugin in your global `opencode.json(c)` to use it in every window.

```jsonc title="~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-acme-plugin"],
}
```

**Settings > Extensions > Plugins** lists them when the app's own server is selected. A plugin's switch turns off only
its desktop UI, and **Reload** loads it again after a failure. To turn off the whole plugin, add `-` and its ID to
`plugins`, for example `"-acme"`.

## Terminal

TUI-only plugins are configured separately and remain active when connected to a remote server.

```json title="cli.json"
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-acme-cli"]
}
```

# Overview

Plugins modify OpenCode's behavior and add new features. A plugin is one package with a server part, a TUI part, a GUI
part, or any combination.

```ts title=".opencode/plugins/example/index.ts"
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.storage.set("loaded", true)
  },
})
```

Migrating an existing OpenCode 1 plugin? Follow the [V1 plugin migration guide](/build/plugins/migrate-v1).

## Parts

Each part is an export of the package. Every part's SDK comes from the one `@opencode/plugin` dependency.

```json title="package.json"
{
  "name": "opencode-acme-plugin",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": "./src/index.ts",
    "./tui": "./src/tui.tsx",
    "./gui-experimental": "./dist/gui-experimental.cjs",
    "./rpc": "./src/rpc.ts"
  },
  "files": ["src", "dist"],
  "dependencies": {
    "@opencode/plugin": "latest"
  }
}
```

- **Server** (`.` or `./server`) runs in the OpenCode server with `@opencode/plugin`. It adds tools, hooks,
  integrations, commands, and agents. See [Server](/build/plugins/server), or [Effect plugins](/build/plugins/effect)
  for the Effect API.
- **TUI** (`./tui`) runs in the terminal UI with `@opencode/plugin/tui`. See [TUI](/build/plugins/cli).
- **GUI** (`./gui-experimental`) runs its `setup` in every OpenCode Desktop window and its `main` in the desktop app's
  main process, with `@opencode/plugin/gui`. See [GUI](/build/plugins/gui).
- **RPC** (`./rpc`) is a typed contract that the server part implements and the other parts and clients call. See
  [RPC](/build/plugins/rpc).

The plugin's `id` comes from its server part's `Plugin.define`. A package with a GUI part and no server part takes its
package name (or a local directory's name) as its `id`. A TUI part declares its own `id`; a GUI part declares none and
takes the plugin's.

## Load

Plugins under `.opencode/plugins/` load automatically, like the local example above. To load published packages or
plugin directories from other locations, add them to `plugins` in `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    "opencode-acme-plugin",
    "opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0",
    "@acme/opencode-plugin",
    "./plugins/local",
    "../shared/plugin",
    "/absolute/path/plugin",
    "file:///home/me/plugins/local",
    {
      "package": "@acme/opencode-plugin",
      "options": {
        "agent": "reviewer",
        "strict": true,
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

- One entry loads every part. The TUI loads the TUI parts of the plugins its server loads, and OpenCode Desktop loads
  the GUI parts of the plugins in your global `opencode.json(c)`.
- A package with only a TUI part goes in [`cli.json`](/cli/plugins) instead.
- A local plugin directory with a `package.json` `name` and `exports` loads its parts through them, like the published
  package. Without them, it uses file names at its root: `server` (else `index`), `tui`, and `rpc` with a `.ts`,
  `.tsx`, or `.js` extension, and `gui-experimental.cjs` (or `.js`).
- See [Configure plugins](/plugins) for more loading and configuration options.

## Publish

A published plugin is an npm package with the `package.json` above. Its parts use the same default exports as a local
plugin.

```bash
npm publish
```

- Export `./rpc` when other plugins and clients should import your [RPC contract](/build/plugins/rpc) without loading
  your implementation.
- Build the GUI bundle before you publish, and include it through `files`. See
  [Build the bundle](/build/plugins/gui#build-the-bundle).
- Use versions compatible with the OpenCode release you target, and test the installed package, not only a
  workspace-linked copy. Publish a compatible plugin update when you adopt a newer API contract.
